questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right to livelihood was held to be part of the right to life under Article 21 in:

options.A: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
options.B: I.C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)
options.C: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
options.D: Kharak Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others (1962)

questions.explanation: Pavement dwellers could not be evicted without a fair procedure, since deprivation of livelihood deprives them of life.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The 'instrumentality or agency of the State' test for determining who is 'State' under Article 12 was laid down in:

options.A: Sukhdev Singh v. Bhagatram Sardar Singh
options.B: University of Madras v. Santa Bai
options.C: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
options.D: Pradeep Kumar Biswas v. Indian Institute of Chemical Biology

questions.explanation: Ajay Hasia (1981) laid down tests such as State financial support, deep and pervasive control and functional character.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The balance and harmony between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles was held to be a basic feature in:

options.A: Waman Rao v. Union of India (1980)
options.B: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)
options.C: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)
options.D: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan (1965)

questions.explanation: Minerva Mills struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment that gave primacy to Directive Principles over Articles 14 and 19.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The President may seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on a question of law or fact under:
questions.explanation: Article 143 gives advisory jurisdiction; the opinion is not binding on the President.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India can be removed from office in the same manner as:

options.A: A Judge of the Supreme Court
options.D: The Chief Election Commissioner of India

questions.explanation: Article 148(1) gives the CAG security of tenure equal to a Supreme Court Judge.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a ground for reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech under Article 19(2)?
questions.explanation: Article 19(2) lists sovereignty and integrity, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation and incitement to an offence.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in:

options.A: Domestic work performed in their own homes
options.B: Agricultural work on their family's own farms

questions.explanation: Article 24 is part of the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23 and 24).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The number of languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is:
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule has 22 languages after the 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures is vested by Article 324 in:

options.C: The Ministry of Law and Justice

questions.explanation: Article 324 creates an independent Election Commission.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A resolution to impeach the President under Article 61 must be passed by a majority of:

options.A: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
options.B: A simple majority of the House
options.C: Three-fourths of the total membership of the House
options.D: Two-thirds of the total membership of the House

questions.explanation: Notice of at least fourteen days, signed by one-fourth of the House members, is also required.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions is guaranteed by:
questions.explanation: Article 30(1) protects the choice of minorities, whether based on religion or language.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 248, the residuary power of legislation vests in:
questions.explanation: Matters not enumerated in the State or Concurrent Lists fall under Parliament's exclusive power.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The principle of collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha is contained in:
questions.explanation: A vote of no confidence against one minister is treated as a vote against the whole Council.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The famous movement 'from status to contract' in the evolution of societies was described by:
questions.explanation: Maine's Ancient Law (1861) traced a shift from fixed status relations to freely negotiated contracts.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The 'veil of ignorance' and the 'original position' are devices used in the theory of justice of:
questions.explanation: In A Theory of Justice, Rawls reasons about principles chosen behind a veil of ignorance.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The classification of law into eternal, natural, divine and human law is associated with:
questions.explanation: Aquinas, in Summa Theologica, linked human law to natural law and reason.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The interest theory of rights, treating law as a protection of social interests, was advanced by:
questions.explanation: Jhering emphasised that law serves social purposes and protects interests.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In Pramatha Nath Mullick v. Pradyumna Kumar Mullick, the Privy Council recognised that a Hindu idol is:

options.A: Only a trust without legal personality
options.B: A res nullius belonging to the State
options.D: A natural person with full capacity

questions.explanation: The idol is a juristic person; its interests are managed by a shebait.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The two essential elements of possession in law are:

options.A: Locus standi and cause of action

questions.explanation: Corpus is physical control and animus is the intention to hold as one's own.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an essential of a valid custom as a source of law?
questions.explanation: A custom must be ancient, certain, continuous, reasonable and not opposed to public policy; legislative approval is not required.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v. Boots Cash Chemists, the display of goods on shelves was held to be:
questions.explanation: The customer makes the offer at the cash desk, and the shopkeeper may accept or refuse it.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 4 of the Indian Contract Act, communication of acceptance is complete as against the proposer when:

options.A: It is read by the proposer
options.B: It is reduced to writing and registered with a notary public
options.D: It is put in transmission beyond the acceptor's power

questions.explanation: The postal rule: acceptance binds the proposer once posted, but binds the acceptor only on reaching the proposer.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 20 of the Indian Contract Act, an agreement is void where both parties are under:

options.A: A mistake as to a point of Indian law
options.B: A mistake as to the market price of goods
options.C: A mistake as to a fact essential to the agreement
options.D: A mistake as to the other party's motives

questions.explanation: Bilateral mistake of fact makes the agreement void, but mistake of Indian law does not.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Anticipatory breach of contract was recognised in the case of:

options.C: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.

questions.explanation: The innocent party may sue at once when the other renounces the contract before performance is due.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, where a sum is named as payable on breach, the aggrieved party is entitled to:

options.A: The entire sum named, as a penalty
options.B: No compensation if loss is not proved
options.C: Reasonable compensation up to the amount named
options.D: Only the actual loss proved with no limit

questions.explanation: Indian law does not distinguish between liquidated damages and penalty; courts award reasonable compensation.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 128 of the Contract Act, the liability of a surety is, unless otherwise provided:

options.A: Secondary and arising only after a court judgment
options.B: Limited to half of the debt
options.D: Co-extensive with that of the principal debtor

questions.explanation: The creditor can proceed against the surety without first suing the principal debtor.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: The maxim 'nemo dat quod non habet', reflected in Section 27 of the Sale of Goods Act, means that:

options.A: Every seller must deliver the goods before payment
options.B: A seller can never recover the price
options.C: A buyer must inspect the goods before purchase
options.D: No one can give a better title than he has

questions.explanation: Subject to exceptions such as sale by a mercantile agent or estoppel, a non-owner cannot pass good title.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Private nuisance is an unlawful interference with a person's:
questions.explanation: It includes smells, noise and vibrations that unreasonably affect neighbours.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In tort, 'assault' consists of:

options.B: Creating apprehension of immediate harmful contact

questions.explanation: Battery requires actual contact; assault requires only the reasonable fear of it.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The essential element of false imprisonment, as shown in Bird v. Jones, is:

options.A: Total restraint of the person's liberty
options.B: Physical injury caused to the plaintiff by the defendant

questions.explanation: Partial restraint, where there is a reasonable means of escape, is not false imprisonment.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Which of the following is an essential of the tort of malicious prosecution?

options.A: Conviction of the plaintiff by the trial court
options.B: Pendency of the prosecution against the plaintiff
options.C: Prosecution ending in favour of the plaintiff

questions.explanation: The plaintiff must also prove absence of reasonable and probable cause, malice, and damage.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Nichols v. Marsland, the defendants escaped liability because the flood was caused by:
questions.explanation: Extraordinary rainfall not reasonably foreseeable amounted to an act of God.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The standard of care of a doctor in negligence under the Bolam test is that of:

options.A: An ordinary person on the street
options.B: A reasonable body of medical opinion
options.D: The most skilled specialist in the field

questions.explanation: A doctor is not negligent if he acts in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of medical men.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 contains a total of:
questions.explanation: The BNS has 358 sections; the BNSS has 531 and the BSA has 170.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: In the stages of a crime, which of the following is generally NOT punishable?
questions.explanation: Preparation is punishable only where the law specifically provides, as in preparing to wage war.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Criminal conspiracy is dealt with in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 61 BNS corresponds to Section 120A and 120B IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Cheating is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 318 corresponds to Sections 415 and 420 IPC; Section 316 deals with criminal breach of trust.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Abetment of suicide is punishable under which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 108 corresponds to Section 306 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Where A aims to kill B but accidentally kills C, A's liability is explained by the doctrine of:
questions.explanation: Malice is transferred from the intended victim to the actual victim.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Which of the following amounts to 'grievous hurt'?

options.A: A minor cut on the finger of the hand
options.B: A bruise on the forearm of the victim
options.C: Temporary swelling of the cheek and lip
options.D: Permanent loss of sight of one eye

questions.explanation: Grievous hurt includes emasculation, permanent privation of sight or hearing, fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: 'Mens rea' is generally NOT required for an offence that is of:
questions.explanation: Strict liability offences, usually regulatory in nature, do not require proof of a guilty mind.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 10 of the CPC, 1908 bars a court from proceeding with a suit where:

options.A: The plaintiff seeks only declaratory relief without consequential relief
options.B: The suit is filed after the limitation period has run out
options.C: The matter is directly in issue in an earlier pending suit
options.D: The defendant fails to appear on the date fixed

questions.explanation: Section 10 codifies the rule of res sub judice to prevent multiplicity of proceedings.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A 'necessary party' in a civil suit is one:

options.A: Who has no interest in the subject matter
options.B: Whose presence is merely convenient to the court
options.C: Who is named by the court as an observer
options.D: Without whom no effective decree can be passed

questions.explanation: A proper party is one whose presence helps in complete adjudication, but whose absence does not defeat the decree.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: An application to set aside an ex parte decree under Order IX Rule 13 CPC must be made within:

options.A: Thirty days from the date of the decree
options.B: Fifteen days from the date of decree
options.C: Sixty days from the date of the decree
options.D: Ninety days from the date of decree

questions.explanation: The period is thirty days from the date of the decree, or from knowledge where summons was not duly served.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The power of a civil court to review its own decree is conferred by:
questions.explanation: Review lies on discovery of new evidence, mistake apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under the BNSS, 2023, information of a cognizable offence given by electronic communication must be signed by the informant within:
questions.explanation: This provision allows e-FIRs, which are recorded on being signed within three days.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under the BNSS, 2023, the court must pronounce judgment in a criminal trial within how many days of the conclusion of arguments?
questions.explanation: The BNSS fixes the time limit to speed up trials, with a possible extension for written reasons.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides for the exclusion of time spent:

options.A: In obtaining the legal opinion of an advocate on merits
options.B: Bona fide prosecuting a case in a wrong court
options.C: In waiting for the opponent's reply to a notice
options.D: On negotiating a settlement outside the court

questions.explanation: The plaintiff must have acted in good faith and with due diligence.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The principle 'bail is the rule and jail is the exception' was laid down in:

options.B: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar
options.C: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

questions.explanation: Justice Krishna Iyer stated this principle in Balchand (1977); courts must consider gravity, flight risk and tampering of evidence.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act, the burden of proving a fact especially within the knowledge of a person lies on:
questions.explanation: Section 106 (Section 109 BSA) does not relieve the prosecution of its primary burden.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: 'Conclusive proof' means that:

options.A: The fact is proved only by documents and records
options.B: The court may presume the fact until it is disproved by evidence
options.C: The court must regard it as proved, allowing no disproof
options.D: The fact must be proved beyond reasonable doubt

questions.explanation: Conclusive proof bars any evidence to the contrary.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Primary evidence of a document means:

options.A: The original document itself, produced in court
options.B: A certified copy issued by a competent public officer
options.C: A copy made from the original by a mechanical process
options.D: An oral account of its contents

questions.explanation: Copies and oral accounts are secondary evidence, allowed only in specified situations.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Facts of which the court takes 'judicial notice':

options.B: Must be proved by two witnesses
options.D: Are proved only by expert opinion

questions.explanation: Section 57 of the Evidence Act lists facts which courts must judicially notice, such as laws in force in India.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: A 'reservation' to a treaty is a statement made by a State that purports to:

options.A: Seek the prior approval of the UN Security Council
options.B: Exclude or modify the effect of some provisions
options.D: Terminate the treaty on all parties

questions.explanation: Article 2(1)(d) of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, 1969 defines reservation; it must not be incompatible with the treaty's object and purpose.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The 'constitutive theory' of recognition holds that a State becomes a State:

options.A: Only through recognition by other States
options.B: Only on admission to the United Nations
options.C: Automatically on fulfilling the criteria of statehood
options.D: Only after a plebiscite in its territory

questions.explanation: The declaratory theory, in contrast, says recognition merely acknowledges an existing State.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The rule of 'double criminality' in extradition requires that the act be:

options.B: An offence in both the requesting and requested State
options.C: Punishable only by death in either State
options.D: A political offence in the requesting or requested State

questions.explanation: Extradition is generally denied unless the conduct is criminal in both jurisdictions.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The number of non-permanent members of the UN Security Council is:
questions.explanation: The Council has fifteen members: five permanent and ten elected non-permanent members serving two-year terms.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The number of Geneva Conventions adopted in 1949 on the protection of victims of war is:
questions.explanation: They cover wounded soldiers on land, shipwrecked sailors, prisoners of war and civilians.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Universal jurisdiction in international law is traditionally exercised over:
questions.explanation: Pirates are regarded as enemies of all mankind (hostis humani generis), permitting any State to prosecute them.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: The Dayabhaga school of Hindu law is mainly followed in:
questions.explanation: Dayabhaga differs from Mitakshara in that sons do not acquire a right by birth in ancestral property.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: In Muslim law, 'Ijma' refers to:

options.A: Reasoning by analogy from the Quran
options.B: The consensus of jurists on a point of law
options.C: The customs of a particular locality or tribe

questions.explanation: The four main sources are the Quran, Sunnah, Ijma and Qiyas.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the minimum age of the bridegroom is:
questions.explanation: Section 5(iii) sets the age at 21 for males and 18 for females.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Special Marriage Act, 1954, public notice of the intended marriage must be given for:
questions.explanation: Objections may be raised within thirty days, after which the marriage can be solemnised.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift of immovable property must be made by:

options.A: A will executed by the donor at the time of death
options.B: An unregistered note signed by the donee and one witness
options.C: A registered instrument attested by two witnesses
options.D: An oral declaration made before the donee

questions.explanation: Section 123 requires registration and attestation by at least two witnesses.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: In a usufructuary mortgage, the mortgagee:

options.A: Acquires title immediately on repayment of the whole loan amount
options.B: Has no right to possession of the property
options.C: Takes possession and the rents in lieu of interest
options.D: Can sell the property on default without a court

questions.explanation: Under Section 58(d) TPA, the mortgagee may recover the debt from the rents and profits.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The first compulsory licence in India under the Patents Act, 1970 was granted for the drug:
questions.explanation: The Controller granted it to Natco Pharma in 2012 against Bayer's patent on Nexavar.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The tort of 'passing off' mainly protects:

options.A: The design of an industrial article or product
options.B: Goodwill attached to an unregistered mark
options.C: The copyright of a literary work
options.D: A patent granted by the State

questions.explanation: A passing off action lies where a defendant misrepresents his goods or services as those of the plaintiff.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: In T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India, the Supreme Court gave the word 'forest' under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980:

options.A: A meaning limited to notified national parks and sanctuaries
options.B: A meaning limited to reserved forests
options.C: Its dictionary meaning, regardless of ownership
options.D: A meaning limited to State-owned land

questions.explanation: The Court extended protection to all areas recorded as forest, irrespective of ownership or classification.

questions.subject: Company Law
questions.question: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, a covered company must spend on CSR at least:

options.B: 2% of its average net profits of the preceding three years
options.C: 5% of its net profit of the current financial year alone
options.D: 1% of its turnover in the preceding year

questions.explanation: The CSR obligation applies to companies meeting thresholds of net worth, turnover or net profit.

questions.subject: Administrative Law
questions.question: In re Delhi Laws Act (1951), the Supreme Court held that the legislature cannot delegate:

options.B: Its power to make rules and regulations
options.C: Its power to frame administrative details
options.D: Its power to fix dates for commencement

questions.explanation: Delegation is allowed, but essential legislative policy must be laid down by the legislature itself.

questions.subject: Consumer Law
questions.question: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the 2021 Rules, the National Commission hears complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration exceeds:
questions.explanation: The District Commission hears up to fifty lakh, and the State Commission fifty lakh to two crore.

questions.subject: Banking & Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, after receipt of a demand notice for a dishonoured cheque, the drawer must pay within:
questions.explanation: The notice must be given within thirty days of receiving information of dishonour; failure to pay attracts prosecution.

questions.subject: Information Technology Law
questions.question: Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides to intermediaries:

options.D: Immunity only for the government and its agencies

questions.explanation: The safe harbour is lost if the intermediary fails to observe due diligence or to act on actual knowledge.

questions.subject: Legal Services
questions.question: An award made by a Lok Adalat under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:

options.A: Needs a fresh trial for enforcement
options.B: Is only a recommendation without any legal effect
options.C: Is deemed to be a decree of a civil court
options.D: Can be appealed to the High Court

questions.explanation: The award is final and binding, and no appeal lies against it.

questions.subject: Human Rights Law
questions.question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on:
questions.explanation: 10 December is observed every year as Human Rights Day.
